Against the T2R3 anchor: rel_l2 +1.90 % of error WORSE where the 3-vs-3 said -4.4 % (a 4.0-pp instrument residual, the largest on record), tke -1.40 % against -3.53 % predicted, sps +0.440 against +0.95. Latency was the other half: 8.69 board ms against 4.78 (-0.207 final) -- the staging README's '1.28 ms/step' was wrong, the build log says 5.457 (3.629 with TF32 on), because U-FNO is conv-heavy at batch 1 and allow_tf32=False makes its 3x3 convs ~50 % slower. Working hypothesis: U-FNO's local advantage is in-distribution memorization -- the interior Re-band k-fold, the only instrument that called T2R3's shape, was never run on it. Every non-FNO family is gated on that k-fold now. The Track-1 twin is WITHDRAWN.

Against R16 (the same 8 w96 FOUR-layer members on this board) the change is DEPTH at dropout 0.45; against T2R5 -- the do30 L8x4 archive going up on Track 2 the same day, same depth, same member count, same single fused invocation -- the only difference is the dropout the members were TRAINED with, which Q4's five-set 3-vs-3 measured at EXACTLY 0.00 full-split sps (43.98 vs 43.98) and +0.13 on the proxy. Equal FLOPs, equal score -- 4xL8 and 8xL4 sit on one accuracy-per-FLOP frontier, which is the reading the round was staged to get. The prediction over-read tke (+0.353 predicted, +0.202 delivered) and sps (+0.138 predicted, +0.066 delivered): the FNO-family proxy is 1-2 pp optimistic in the direction of the change, as it was for w96. THE PAIR IS NOT THE A/B IT WAS STAGED AS: the Track-2 slot went up with the do45 twin, not the staged do30 archive, so R17/T2R5 became the FIFTH cross-track identity check instead of the dropout-at-depth reading.
